summary: The contrast is structural: I.2 basəm-le has an l-coded experiencer and a stimulus subject (with possible l-NP doubling); I.3 basəm lebe has heart as subject and may have b-marked grounds. II.1 causes pleasure to a person or heart. Do not infer argument coding from free German/English renderings.

Finite taste/maturation is independently supported by JTM 1.1/5 and 94/135. Numerous basimo adjectives corroborate culinary evaluation but are not proof of a verbal Part act.; greetings, weather, prosperous condition, stories, games and reconciliation span the adjective’s range.

Qaṭəl occurs in changes and continuing evaluations. Infectum-wa at 58/76 is irrealis; at 11/236 it is habitual. The existing II Detransitive Infectum (LB 162 = Talay 1/162) denotes rejoicing with a companion, not an external agent acting on the subject.

II fine ploughing is established by the explicit agricultural sequence in two Midyat contexts. Infinitiv bəsomano is retained under the reader’s analysis; no claim of etymological derivation from the agricultural sense is made.
56/128 has lebe in the supplied verse versus leba in the inherited example; this is an unresolved source discrepancy, not a licensed fix-text correction.
Repeated story evaluations and closing formulae are lexical-adjective evidence and are not multiplied as verbal examples. At 96/304 the alignment warning blocks quotation of the German translation.

The head-pleasantness prayer at MAC NE Mother Mary saves Sultan’s son/15 has a conventional condolence function in its death context. It is included as a phrase, not a new verbal sense or a Part act. example; compare the more general good-spirits farewell at 44/166.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. English accompanying the added examples is the supplied project machine translation, copied and cut without retranslation; lexical decisions rest on the Turoyo.
Experiencer coding is not transitive 'enjoy': Jan 3.17/276 has fronted patriarch experiencer resumed by -le and voice stimulus. I.3 instead takes a rejoicing collective or heart as subject.
Jan 1.42/1844 contrasts II caused-pleasure commands with active friendly interaction using ʕam; one repeated verse supplies only one independent construction attestation.
Auditory basəm comparative with m- and past copula at Jan 2.32/5289 may be lexical adjective evidence, as related round-1 examples already caution. No new Part act. box is introduced.
Jan 3.17/292 switches into learned Syriac; it illustrates register and the cognate dative pattern, without proving a Turoyo form.

Should lexical basimo/basəmto/basime be included in a verbal Part act. box under the editors’ policy? They are excluded from new verbal boxes here, while the reciprocal idiom is explicitly adjectival.
Verify lebe versus leba at 56/128, and the shortened II Imperativ basám at MAC NE Mem and Zin/34.
At 66/7, confirm the girl as object -o- and the ruler as experiencer in b-lebe. At 64/8, determine the agent and object of mbasamme before adding an example.
Does 66/114 describe pleasant weather or a rejoicing traveller? The German favours the latter; no unambiguous sense assignment was possible.
Check comparative basəm at Talay 1/222 and 58/111, basəm yo at 69/428, and -yo in basəmliyo at 63/95.
Is mbasam ruḥe b- conventional social ingratiation or contextual self-comfort? Only one attestation is available.
At 96/304 the translation is flagged for a hunting/housework subject mismatch. Verify the edition before quoting it; no translation from that occurrence has been added.
Jan 1.42/1844: confirm whether mbasamlan aʕmayye conventionally means conciliatory friendly interaction or an elliptical form of making their hearts glad; the proposed 1c rests on one passage.
Jan 1.16/720: is b- a productive experiencer marker with bosəm, or does it mean pleasant work among people?
Jan 2.31/5172: explain masculine Basəmle with feminine i šanṯo, including possible impersonal construction or transcription issue.
Jan 2.32/5289: confirm adjectival comparative basəm mu qolo rather than finite Preterit Intransitive.
Correct English past-tense typo: feel → fell
rationale: The sentence narrates Kayalo lying down and falling asleep. English requires 'fell asleep'; the supplied edition translation ends 'er schläft ein'.

summary: Food, places, speech and nominalised actions all occur as stimuli with l-coded experiencers; gustatory liking retains this frame.
Favourable ecological conditions of a home locality extend pleasant weather/place quality; no separate restoration sense.
Musical performance at 64/8 remains a possible participant extension, but agent/object segmentation is unresolved.
Improvement of ḥal of Midyat inhabitants supports the round-1 ecological/prosperity extension without a new sense.
ban noše expresses experiencers of pleasant work; compare l-coded experiencers elsewhere. The exact b- construction requires confirmation.
Pleasure caused to hearts can pragmatically calm or reassure. Repeated commands and later comfort remain covered by the retained sense.
